_comment: aplayermode.com Pinterest daily drip queue (owner-approved 16 Oct 2026). config.pins_per_day is THE release rate. The Worker (workers/aplayermode-com/src/pinqueue.js buildPinfeedXml) serves /pinfeed.xml from this file at request time: the 5 launch items plus every variant whose release_date <= today in America/Chicago, newest config.max_feed_items; no deploy per day. channel + launch are derived from config/aplayermode_pinfeed.json; variants come from config/aplayermode_routines.json via scripts/aplayermode/pin_queue.mjs (weekly: scripts/aplayermode/weekly_pin_drip.sh, Mondays in the Daily Citation Intelligence lane). Guarded by validate:aplayermode-pinterest and tests/aplayermode/pinqueue.test.mjs.

log.why: 1 a day on one board: 21 pins, 5 monthly profile views, 0 measured visits (Pinterest, 1 Nov 2026); Pinterest distributes fresh pins and 3 a day stays far under the 200-a-day auto-publish cap. Stop rule from the Growth playbook: 0 clicks at 4 weeks -> new format, 8 weeks -> pause

config.held_comment: A variant with a 'held' block is never dated or put in a feed (workers/aplayermode-com/src/pinqueue.js isHeld). While hold_new_pins is true, refills are planned held too. Release (one command): docs/OPERATIONS.md, 'Releasing held A Player Mode pins'.

boards._comment: Pinterest topic boards (owner-approved 1 Nov 2026). Pinterest auto-publish maps ONE feed to ONE board, so each board has its own feed, served by the aplayermode-com Worker (/pinfeed.xml = the first board, /pinfeed/<slug>.xml the others). A pin's board is its page section. Pins released before split_from all went to the first board and stay there. keywords: Pinterest search suggestions read 1 Nov 2026; a post-split title naming none is led with the first. 7 Nov 2026: routine pins carry their routine page's slug as section (config/aplayermode_routines.json); 'morning routine', 'adhd morning routine', 'weekly planning', 'weekly reset' and 'sunday reset' added as common Pinterest searches (not re-read in the suggest box), so every routine title starts with one of its board's phrases.

variants.headline: Weekly Founder Scorecard
variants.title: Goal Setting: A Weekly Founder Scorecard
variants.description: A weekly founder scorecard for goal setting: this week's key number, one thing shipped, conversations with customers, the biggest blocker, what you will stop doing and next week's one outcome.

variants.headline: Time Blindness Morning Routine
points: A clock you can see in every room
variants.title: Morning Routine for Time Blindness: Clocks, Timers and a Leave Alarm
variants.description: A morning routine for time blindness: a visible clock in every room, a timer on the shower, one alarm for shoes on and one for leave now, the same order every day, and the plan counted back from the time you have to leave. Not medical advice.

variants.headline: Weekly Review Questions
points: When is my first focus block?
variants.title: Weekly Planning Review: 6 Questions in 10 Minutes
variants.description: Six weekly review questions that take ten minutes: what got done, what slipped and why, what you promised people, what you can drop, next week's three outcomes and when your first focus block is.

variants.headline: Time Blocking, Changing Days
points: Fit it in the biggest gap
variants.title: Time Blocking When Every Day Is Different
variants.description: Time blocking when no two days look alike: plan tomorrow the night before, place the fixed things first, pick one must-do, fit it into the biggest gap, keep everything else on a list and re-plan once at lunch.

variants.headline: Minimum Viable Day Checklist
variants.title: Productivity Checklist for a Minimum Viable Day
variants.description: A minimum viable day checklist: food, water and sleep, one work task, one home task, one kind word to someone, no new commitments, and when those are done the day is done.

variants.headline: Family Gratitude Routine
points: A gratitude jar on the counter
variants.title: Gratitude Routine for Families That Takes 2 Minutes
variants.description: A family gratitude routine that takes two minutes: ask for the best part of the day at dinner, write one thank-you note a week, keep a gratitude jar on the counter, name one thing at bedtime, listen without fixing and keep it short.

variants.headline: End-of-Day Shutdown
variants.title: Productivity: An End-of-Day Shutdown Routine
variants.description: A ten-minute end-of-day shutdown routine: write what got done, move unfinished tasks, pick tomorrow's first task, clear the desk, close every tab and say done for today.

variants.headline: Work-From-Home Morning Routine
variants.title: ADHD Morning Routine for Working From Home
variants.description: An ADHD-friendly work-from-home morning: dressed for outside, a desk cleared the night before, coffee then one hard task, messages only after 45 minutes, a stand-up break at 10 and lunch away from the desk.

variants.headline: Weekly Planner, No Overplanning
points: Only a top task each day
variants.title: Weekly Planner Routine Without Overplanning
variants.description: Plan the week without overplanning: one page instead of a planner spread, three outcomes only, fixed things first, empty space every day, just a top task for each day, and stop after 20 minutes.

variants.headline: Time Blocking for Deep Work
variants.title: Time Blocking for Deep Work: 6 Rules
variants.description: Six rules for deep-work time blocks: the phone in another room, one task per block, 90 minutes then a break, the same time each day, your status set to busy and a note of where you stopped.

variants.headline: Tired Day Productivity
variants.title: Productivity on a Tired Day: What to Move and What to Keep
variants.description: Productivity on a tired day: the hardest thing before noon, move one meeting, short tasks after lunch, a ten-minute walk outside, no big decisions today and an early night.

variants.headline: Family Mental Load Routine
points: Each owns tasks start to end
variants.title: Family Routine for Sharing the Mental Load
variants.description: A family routine for sharing the mental load: write every open loop down, split the list in two, each person owns tasks from start to finish, the calendar holds the reminders, sync for ten minutes on Sunday and swap one job a month.

variants.headline: Founder Follow-Up Routine
points: List who you owe a reply
variants.title: Productivity: A Follow-Up Routine for Busy Founders
variants.description: A follow-up routine for busy founders: list who you owe a reply, answer three before noon, put every promise on the calendar, keep answers to two lines, clear the rest on Friday so nothing waits on memory.

variants.headline: Morning Routine With Kids
points: Shoes and bags by the door
Two calm minutes in the car
variants.title: Morning Routine With Kids When You Have ADHD
variants.description: A morning routine for ADHD parents: lunches packed the night before, shoes and bags by the door, a picture checklist for each child, your coffee before their breakfast, one leave-time alarm for everyone and two calm minutes in the car.

variants.headline: Monday Weekly Planning
variants.title: Weekly Planning on Monday Morning in 15 Minutes
variants.description: A Monday morning weekly planning routine that takes 15 minutes: open the calendar before the inbox, note what changed since Friday, pick three outcomes, book them into real slots, tell people what you will deliver and start outcome one.

variants.headline: Daily Routine, Chaotic Day
variants.title: Daily Routine for a Chaotic Day: Keep One Thing Moving
variants.description: A daily routine for chaotic days: write down the three fixed things, pick one thing that must move, do it before noon, batch the small tasks, say no to one request and end with tomorrow's first step.

variants.headline: Habit Tracker for Restarting
points: Tick a box, no streak score
variants.title: Habit Tracker for Restarting: 2 Habits, Not 10
variants.description: A habit tracker for restarting: choose two habits instead of ten, use the smallest version of each, do them at the same time every day, tick a box without a streak score, never miss twice and review on Sundays.

variants.headline: Family Admin Routine
variants.title: Family Admin Routine: 30 Minutes a Month
variants.description: A monthly family admin routine: check bills and renewals, list upcoming birthdays, book appointments, collect school forms and dates, cancel unused subscriptions, all in 30 minutes on the first Sunday of the month.
